{"alias_target":null,"confidence":"high","current_chinese":"\"我们三个面色惨白地坐着，仿佛刚刚目睹了一场肮脏而恶毒的谋杀。至少如果我们看的是谋杀，那个凶手也不会像眼下这样面无表情地直视着我们的眼睛。或许是那种冷酷而不为所动的傲慢感让我们如此不安。但无论我们试图将什么恶毒的情感强加到那只蜥蜴身上，我们都知道那根本不是蜥蜴的情感，而只是我们自己的。蜥蜴只不过在以简单直接的蜥蜴方式做它蜥蜴该做的事。它对那种恐惧、那种愧疚、那种羞耻、那种丑陋——我们这些唯一懂得愧疚和羞耻的动物试图强加给它的东西——一无所知。于是这一切都反弹回到我们身上，仿佛反射在它那只目光坚定而超然的眼睛的镜面中。\"\n    -Douglas Adams, \"Last Chance to See\". 1990.","current_english":"“The three of us were sitting ashen faced as if we had just witnessed a foul\n and malignant murder. At least if we had been watching a murder the murderer\n wouldn't have been looking us impassively in the eye as he did it. Maybe it\n was the feeling of cold unflinching arrogance that so disturbed us. But\n whatever malign emotions we tried to pin on to the lizard, we knew that they\n weren't the lizard's emotions at all, only ours. The lizard was simply going\n about its lizardly business in a simple, straightforward lizardly way. It\n didn't know anything about the horror, the guilt, the shame, the ugliness that\n we, uniquely guilty and ashamed animals, were trying to foist on it. So we got\n it all straight back at us, as if reflected in the mirror of its single\n unwavering and disinterested eye.”\n    -Douglas Adams, “Last Chance to See”. 1990.","decision_authority":"Current docs/decisions.md literary exceptions; full rereview explicitly distinguishes quotations from gameplay terminology.","deferral_owner":null,"deferral_reason":null,"dependency_group":"Non-unique monsters","display_context":"QuoteDB literary quotation for entity/help display; aliases resolve within the current language namespace before unwrap_desc.","evidence_locations":["crawl-ref/source/dat/descript/quotes.txt:3310","crawl-ref/source/dat/descript/zh/quotes.txt:2797","crawl-ref/source/database.cc@getQuoteString","crawl-ref/source/libutil.cc@unwrap_desc"],"fact_sha256":"0b90e28627248f95b70d224da1625980c4e5622c083f57db3ca4b26181a606d7","glossary_authority":"docs/glossary.md SHA-256 8a36accf4fc362bf8f103d84ba5d5e6639615274e94d38b16a2d2afe0b0c04cf","identity":"quotes:komodo dragon","key":"komodo dragon","lifecycle":"direct-quote","literary_exception_reason":null,"producer_consumer":"database.cc QuoteDB loader and getQuoteString -> unwrap_desc; describe.cc / ability.cc / mutation.cc / lookup-help.cc use canonical English lookup keys.","proposed_translation":null,"reentry_trigger":"Re-review when this quotation, attribution, alias target, literary terminology decision, or display consumer changes.","rejected_alternatives":["未将文学引文强制套入同名游戏机制或实体；非阻断风格建议保留。"],"resolved_key":"komodo dragon","reviewer_rationale":"三人看蜥蜴进食误赋谋杀恶情/认识冷然只是动物、恐惭镜返人类的整段心理论证与单眼意象完整。","section":"Non-unique monsters","suggestions":[],"terminal_conclusion":"keep"}
{"alias_target":null,"confidence":"high","current_chinese":"\"……克拉肯，亦称蟹鱼，据挪威的引水人说，并没有那么大，因为头和尾巴加在一起，也不比我们的厄兰岛宽多少（即不足16公里）……它栖息在海底，周身始终环绕着无数小鱼，这些小鱼既是它的食物，也反过来受它喂养：因为它的进食——如果我记得E. 蓬托皮丹的记载没错的话——持续时间不超过三个月，之后又需要三个月来消化。它的排泄物随后滋养了一大群小鱼，因此渔夫们会探测它的栖息之处……渐渐地，克拉肯升到海面，当它在十到十二英寻深时，船只最好撤离其附近，因为不久之后它便会破水而出，像一座浮动的岛屿，从它那可怕的鼻孔中喷出水流，掀起环状的巨浪，能够波及数英里之远。谁能怀疑这就是约伯记中的利维坦呢？\"\n    -Jacob Wallenberg, \"Min son på galejan\". 1781.","current_english":"“... Kraken, also called the Crab-fish, which [according to the pilots of\n Norway] is not that huge, for heads and tails counted, he is no larger than\n our Öland is wide [i.e. less than 16 km] ... He stays at the sea floor,\n constantly surrounded by innumerable small fishes, who serve as his food and\n are fed by him in return: for his meal, if I remember correctly what E.\n Pontoppidan writes, lasts no longer than three months, and another three are\n then needed to digest it. {"alias_target":null,"confidence":"high","current_chinese":"\"当然，若我们将龙或林德虫想象为这样一种怪兽——它长长的脖颈末端长着鹰头、狮头或海豚头；宽阔的背上长着狮鹫或纳希翼；在层层盘卷的尾巴上长着带倒钩的毒刺；口吐火焰；爱上少女并将她们掳走；时而化作这种形态，时而变作那种；盘踞在辛苦积攒的财宝之上——简而言之，若将其想象为一头拥有寓言赋予它的一切特征的怪兽，那么相信龙和林德虫便是疯狂的。但若我们仅仅将它视为一种可怕的、如今已从我们大陆上灭绝的怪兽，那么对它存在的信念便毫无可笑之处。\"\n    -Leopold Ziegelhauſer, _Schattenbilder der Vorzeit: Ein Kranz von\n     Geschichten, Sagen, Legenden, Märchen, Skizzen und Heldenmahlen, Aus allen\n     Gegenden Deutschlands und des österreichischen Kaiserstaates_. 1844.","current_english":"“Freilich verbürgt uns keine Silbe die Existenz von solcherlei Thieren, wenn\n wir uns den Drachen oder Lindwurm als ein Ungeheuer vorstellen, dessen langer\n Hals in einen Adler-, Löwen- oder Delphinenkopf endigt; das auf dem breiten\n Rücken Greifs- oder Nachisittige trägt; und am vielfach\n gerollten Schweif einen Stachel mit Widerhaken hat; Feuer speit; sich in\n Mädchen verliebt und diese entführt; bald diese bald jene Gestalt annimmt; auf\n sauer erworbenen Schatzen ruht — kurz, als ein Ungeheuer, das alle\n Eigenschaften besitzt, welche die Fabel ihm andichtet; dann wäre es Wahnsinn,\n an Drachen und Lindwürmer glauben zu wollen. Nehmen wir aber dafür bloß ein\n furchtbares Ungeheuer überhaupt, welches nun aus unserem Welttheile vertilgt\n ist, so hat der Glaube daran nichts Lächerliches.”\n    -Leopold Ziegelhauſer, _Schattenbilder der Vorzeit: Ein Kranz von\n     Geschichten, Sagen, Legenden, Märchen, Skizzen und Heldenmahlen, Aus allen\n     Gegenden Deutschlands und des österreichischen Kaiserstaates_. 1844.","decision_authority":"Current docs/decisions.md literary exceptions; full rereview explicitly distinguishes quotations from gameplay terminology.","deferral_owner":null,"deferral_reason":null,"dependency_group":"Non-unique monsters","display_context":"QuoteDB literary quotation for entity/help display; aliases resolve within the current language namespace before unwrap_desc.","evidence_locations":["crawl-ref/source/dat/descript/quotes.txt:3346","crawl-ref/source/dat/descript/zh/quotes.txt:2811","crawl-ref/source/database.cc@getQuoteString","crawl-ref/source/libutil.cc@unwrap_desc"],"fact_sha256":"3d85fb5523abc52388c87af71595aedfab907359bbbd1942687202c58107811f","glossary_authority":"docs/glossary.md SHA-256 8a36accf4fc362bf8f103d84ba5d5e6639615274e94d38b16a2d2afe0b0c04cf","identity":"quotes:lindwurm","key":"lindwurm","lifecycle":"direct-quote","literary_exception_reason":"The quotation preserves the Germanic creature's proper name.","producer_consumer":"database.cc QuoteDB loader and getQuoteString -> unwrap_desc; describe.cc / ability.cc / mutation.cc / lookup-help.cc use canonical English lookup keys.","proposed_translation":null,"reentry_trigger":"Re-review when this quotation, attribution, alias target, literary terminology decision, or display consumer changes.","rejected_alternatives":["未将文学引文强制套入同名游戏机制或实体；非阻断风格建议保留。"],"resolved_key":"lindwurm","reviewer_rationale":"德文龙颈鹰狮海豚头/翼/钩尾喷火/掳女变形守财、传说俱真则疯/只认灭绝怪物则合理的条件论证完整。","section":"Non-unique monsters","suggestions":[],"terminal_conclusion":"keep"}

{"alias_target":null,"confidence":"high","current_chinese":"\"该死的！让尼普顿劈死你，温斯洛！听啊！听啊，特里同，听啊！咆哮吧，叫我们的父海王从深渊中升起，满怀着狂暴的愤怒！黑色的巨浪翻腾着盐沫，用辛辣的黏液窒息这张年轻的嘴，噎死你，塞满你的器官直到你发青浮肿，被舱底污水和盐水填满，再也不能尖叫——只等他头戴蛤壳冠，拖着黏滑蜿蜒的触手尾和冒着热气的胡须，举起他那可怕的生着鱼鳍的手臂，他那珊瑚齿的三叉戟在风暴中发出女妖般的尖啸，径直刺穿你的喉咙，将你爆开——不再是一团鼓胀的水泡，而是一层爆碎的血色薄膜——一滩虚无，供哈尔庇厄和死去水手的幽灵啄食、抓挠、吞食，最终被那可畏的帝王本人的无尽海水舔食吞咽——从此被所有人遗忘，被所有时间遗忘，被任何神祇或魔鬼遗忘，甚至被大海遗忘，因为温斯洛的任何部分、任何碎片，你灵魂的任何碎屑都不再是温斯洛，而是此刻已然成为大海！\"\n    -Thomas Wake, _The Lighthouse_. 2019","current_english":"“Damn ye! Let Neptune strike ye dead, Winslow! HAAARK! Hark Triton, hark!\n Bellow, bid our father the Sea King rise from the depths full foul in his fury!\n Black waves teeming with salt-foam to smother this young mouth with pungent\n slime, to choke ye, engorging your organs ‘til ye turn blue and bloated with\n bilge and brine and can scream no more -- only when he, crowned in cockle\n shells with slitherin’ tentacled tail and steaming beard take up his fell\n be-finnéd arm, his coral-tine trident screeches banshee-like in the tempest and\n plunges right through yer gullet, bursting ye -- a bulging bladder no more, but\n a blasted bloody film now -- a nothing for the harpies and the souls of dead\n sailors to peck and claw and feed upon, only to be lapped up and swallowed by\n the infinite waters of the dread emperor himself -- forgotten to any man, to\n any time, forgotten to any god or devil, forgotten even to the sea, for any\n stuff or part of Winslow, even any scantling of your soul is Winslow no more,\n but is now itself the sea!”\n    -Thomas Wake, _The Lighthouse_. 2019","decision_authority":"Current docs/decisions.md literary exceptions; {"alias_target":null,"confidence":"high","current_chinese":"\"我们继续划行，进入那高扬歌声所及之处；\n 塞壬很快察觉了我们，我们却未发出声响。\n 她们调好甜美的音调，施下强烈魔力，\n 用这些精妙诗句唱起塞壬之歌：\n '来吧，尤利西斯，举世赞颂的英雄，\n 是你将希腊的荣耀高高托起！\n 停下船来，听听这支歌吧；\n 从未有人经过此地而不侧耳倾听，\n 也无人不心醉神驰地离开，\n 从我们这里获知前所未闻的更多见识。\n 特洛伊广袤土地上发生的一切，\n 希腊人与特洛伊人依诸神旨意\n 在那里承受的一切，我们无不知晓。\n 凡大地所能展现、足以增长\n 人对世间功业的见识，我们尽皆知晓。'\"\n    -Homer, _The Odyssey_, XII, 268-82.\n     trans. George Chapman, 1857.","current_english":"“Row'd on, in reach of an erected voice,\n The Sirens soon took note, without our noise,\n Tuned those sweet accents that made charms so strong,\n And these learn'd numbers made the Sirens' song:\n ‘Come here, thou worthy of a world of praise,\n That dost so high the Grecian glory raise,\n Ulysses! stay thy ship, and that song hear\n That none past ever but it bent his ear,\n But left him ravish'd, and instructed more\n By us, than any ever heard before.\n For we know all things whatsoever were\n In wide Troy labour'd; whatsoever there\n The Grecians and the Trojans both sustain'd\n By those high issues that the Gods ordain'd.\n And whatsoever all the earth can show\n T' inform a knowledge of desert, we know.’”\n    -Homer, _The Odyssey_, XII, 268-82.\n     trans. {"alias_target":null,"confidence":"high","current_chinese":"\"如果突变因此受自然选择的影响，这就意味着任何特定的突变必然朝着对相应物种有利的方向进展；而实际上，化石动物中已知的许多突变例子，显然都是由于这种变化带来的优势所致。然而，我必须在此补充说明，并非所有的突变（就古生物学的意义而言）都归因于自然选择，许多突变并不意味着实际的改良。\"\n    -_Proceedings of the American Philosophical Society_, Volume XXV, no. 150.\n     1896.","current_english":"“If thus mutation is influenced by natural selection, it implies, that any\n particular mutation must advance in a direction advantageous for the\n respective species, and, indeed, many examples of mutation known among fossil\n animals are apparently due to the advantage produced by the change. {"alias_target":null,"confidence":"high","current_chinese":"\"在他们短暂的相处中，斯洛思罗普形成的印象是这只章鱼\n 精神健康状况不佳——尽管他有什么比较的依据呢？但这种\n 软体动物的每一个动作中都有一种疯狂的亢奋，就像当我们\n 对噪音和自己的笨拙格外敏感、不希望东西掉落时，那些\n 无生命的物体偏偏从桌上掉下来——一种'砰！哈哈你听到\n 了吗？又来了，砰！'的感觉——斯洛思罗普终于像掷铁饼\n 一样用尽全身力气把螃蟹抛向大海，得以脱身；而那只章鱼\n 则急切地溅起水花、咕噜作响，紧追不舍，随即消失不见。\"\n    -托马斯·品钦，《万有引力之虹》。1973年。","current_english":"“In their brief time together Slothrop forms the impression that this octopus\n is not in good mental health, though where's his basis for comparing? {"alias_target":null,"confidence":"high","current_chinese":"\"碳酸是构成植物生长起点的三种材料之一，另外两种是水\n 和硝酸。这种酸由碳和氧按一比二的比例化合而成。它是\n 一种无色气体，具有酸味和酸臭；可溶于水；比空气重\n 一半，可以像液体一样从一个容器倒入另一个容器；一百\n 份水可溶解一百零六份这种气体，植物的根系正是由此\n 获得所需的供应。\"\n    -亨利·斯图尔特，《农作物的栽培：农业科学手册与美国\n     农民实用指南》，第十章。1887年。","current_english":"“Carbonic acid is one of the three materials which together form the starting\n point of vegetable growth; the others being water and nitric acid. This acid is\n formed of carbon and oxygen in the proportion of one part of the former to\n two of the latter chemically combined. It is a colorless gas, having an acid\n taste and smell; is soluble in water; weighs one-half more than air and can be\n poured from one vessel to another, as a liquid may be; 100 parts of water\n dissolve 106 parts of this gas, and it is from this source that the roots of\n plants derive the needed supplies of it.”\n    -Henry Stuart, _The Culture of Farm Crops: A Manual of the Science of\n    Agriculture, and a Hand-book of Practice for American Farmers_, ch X. 1887.","decision_authority":"Current docs/decisions.md literary exceptions; full rereview explicitly distinguishes quotations from gameplay terminology.","deferral_owner":null,"deferral_reason":null,"dependency_group":"Non-unique monsters","display_context":"QuoteDB literary quotation for entity/help display; aliases resolve within the current language namespace before unwrap_desc.","evidence_locations":["crawl-ref/source/dat/descript/quotes.txt:3608","crawl-ref/source/dat/descript/zh/quotes.txt:3015","crawl-ref/source/database.cc@getQuoteString","crawl-ref/source/libutil.cc@unwrap_desc"],"fact_sha256":"1975e17725f8982d0345e6c3f2c6d16f72124c85bc310fc419647cce2caf8e54","glossary_authority":"docs/glossary.md SHA-256 8a36accf4fc362bf8f103d84ba5d5e6639615274e94d38b16a2d2afe0b0c04cf","identity":"quotes:oklob plant","key":"oklob plant","lifecycle":"direct-quote","literary_exception_reason":null,"producer_consumer":"database.cc QuoteDB loader and getQuoteString -> unwrap_desc; describe.cc / ability.cc / mutation.cc / lookup-help.cc use canonical English lookup keys.","proposed_translation":null,"reentry_trigger":"Re-review when this quotation, attribution, alias target, literary terminology decision, or display consumer changes.","rejected_alternatives":["未将文学引文强制套入同名游戏机制或实体；非阻断风格建议保留。"],"resolved_key":"oklob plant","reviewer_rationale":"原1887文称carbonic acid气体的历史化学原貌、碳氧1:2/比空气重半/100水溶106气/根取供应数字全保留，不现代纠错史料。","section":"Non-unique monsters","suggestions":[],"terminal_conclusion":"keep"}

{"alias_target":null,"confidence":"high","current_chinese":"\"鬼神话的流行与经久不衰，无疑部分基于这些生物一贯的\n 恶魔特征——这些特征历经岁月而相对恒定：它们是从佛教\n 地狱深渊中涌现的可怕超自然存在，来恐吓邪恶的凡人；\n 它们怪异而凶残的举止和外形令人瞬间生畏；而鬼在日本\n 社会历史与文化档案中的无所不在，则直接归因于鬼的故事\n 所产生的道德、社会和宗教教化作用。\"\n    -诺里科·T·赖德，《日本恶魔传说：从古至今的鬼》，\n     第一章，2010年。","current_english":"“The popularity and longevity of the oni myth is no doubt partially based on\n the beings’ conventional demonic accoutrements, which have remained\n relatively constant through the ages: they are dreadful super-natural\n beings emerging from the abyss of Buddhist hell to terrify wicked mortals;\n their grotesque and savage demeanor and form instill instant fear; and the\n oni’s omnipresence in the socio-historical and cultural archive of Japan is\n directly attributable to the moral, social, and religious edification that\n stories about oni engender.”\n    -Noriko T. {"alias_target":null,"confidence":"high","current_chinese":"\"你所看见的每一颗微小的天球，\n 在运转时无不发出天使般的歌声，\n 永远应和着明眸的天使们的合唱。\"\n    -威廉·莎士比亚，《威尼斯商人》，第五幕第一场。1597年。","current_english":"“There 's not the smallest orb which thou behold'st\n But in his motion like an angel sings,\n Still quiring to the young-eyed cherubins.”\n    -William Shakespeare, _The Merchant of Venice_, V, i. 1597.","decision_authority":"Current docs/decisions.md literary exceptions; full rereview explicitly distinguishes quotations from gameplay terminology.","deferral_owner":null,"deferral_reason":null,"dependency_group":"Non-unique monsters","display_context":"QuoteDB literary quotation for entity/help display; aliases resolve within the current language namespace before unwrap_desc.","evidence_locations":["crawl-ref/source/dat/descript/quotes.txt:3670","crawl-ref/source/dat/descript/zh/quotes.txt:3071","crawl-ref/source/database.cc@getQuoteString","crawl-ref/source/libutil.cc@unwrap_desc"],"fact_sha256":"b87ea327576b496252b945c42f32118eb2d8a4afc36b0be95de7106c3a596cfe","glossary_authority":"docs/glossary.md SHA-256 8a36accf4fc362bf8f103d84ba5d5e6639615274e94d38b16a2d2afe0b0c04cf","identity":"quotes:orb of fire","key":"orb of fire","lifecycle":"direct-quote","literary_exception_reason":null,"producer_consumer":"database.cc QuoteDB loader and getQuoteString -> unwrap_desc; describe.cc / ability.cc / mutation.cc / lookup-help.cc use canonical English lookup keys.","proposed_translation":null,"reentry_trigger":"Re-review when this quotation, attribution, alias target, literary terminology decision, or display consumer changes.","rejected_alternatives":["未将文学引文强制套入同名游戏机制或实体；非阻断风格建议保留。"],"resolved_key":"orb of fire","reviewer_rationale":"微天球运转如天使歌/明眸天使合唱完整，cherubins通用天使非游戏基路伯catalog须直套，莎剧出处保持。","section":"Non-unique monsters","suggestions":[],"terminal_conclusion":"keep"}
{"alias_target":null,"confidence":"high","current_chinese":"\"与此同时，奉至上大能的谕令，\n 插翅使者们以威严的仪式\n 和响彻全军的号角之声宣告\n 即刻在撒旦及其群臣的巍峨都城——\n 万魔殿——召开庄严会议……\"\n    -约翰·弥尔顿，《失乐园》，第一卷，1667年。","current_english":"“Mean while the winged heralds by command\n Of Sovran power, with awful Ceremony\n And Trumpets sound throughout the Host proclaim\n A solemn Councel forthwith to be held\n At Pandaemonium, the high Capital\n Of Satan and his Peers...”\n    -John Milton, _Paradise Lost_, Book I, 1667.","decision_authority":"Current docs/decisions.md literary exceptions; full rereview explicitly distinguishes quotations from gameplay terminology.","deferral_owner":null,"deferral_reason":null,"dependency_group":"Non-unique monsters","display_context":"QuoteDB literary quotation for entity/help display; aliases resolve within the current language namespace before unwrap_desc.","evidence_locations":["crawl-ref/source/dat/descript/quotes.txt:3677","crawl-ref/source/dat/descript/zh/quotes.txt:3078","crawl-ref/source/database.cc@getQuoteString","crawl-ref/source/libutil.cc@unwrap_desc"],"fact_sha256":"3eedcae41d58a67ed4cc04282519ad746494d19c51fa71dc0027392160245208","glossary_authority":"docs/glossary.md SHA-256 8a36accf4fc362bf8f103d84ba5d5e6639615274e94d38b16a2d2afe0b0c04cf","identity":"quotes:pandemonium lord","key":"pandemonium lord","lifecycle":"direct-quote","literary_exception_reason":null,"producer_consumer":"database.cc QuoteDB loader and getQuoteString -> unwrap_desc; describe.cc / ability.cc / mutation.cc / lookup-help.cc use canonical English lookup keys.","proposed_translation":null,"reentry_trigger":"Re-review when this quotation, attribution, alias target, literary terminology decision, or display consumer changes.","rejected_alternatives":["未将文学引文强制套入同名游戏机制或实体；非阻断风格建议保留。"],"resolved_key":"pandemonium lord","reviewer_rationale":"主权令翼使仪号全军宣即刻撒旦群臣在首都庄议、Pandemonium万魔殿名相容当前例外，长句完整。","section":"Non-unique monsters","suggestions":[],"terminal_conclusion":"keep"}

{"alias_target":null,"confidence":"high","current_chinese":"\"我呼唤普罗透斯，\n 执掌钥匙的沧海之主，\n 首生之神，他揭示了\n 万物的起源，\n 将物质变换为\n 千姿百态。\n 受万有敬仰，他通晓智慧，\n 知道现在之事，\n 过去之事，\n 以及未来之事。\n 他掌管一切，\n 其变化远超\n 栖居于白雪皑皑的奥林匹斯、\n 翱翔于天空、\n 跨越大地与海洋的\n 所有不朽者，\n 因为菲西斯最先\n 将万物置于普罗透斯之中。\n 父神啊，在神圣天命的随侍下，\n 请降临于秘仪的信徒，\n 为勤劳富足的一生\n 带来善终。\"\n    -《俄耳甫斯赞美诗》，第二十五首。\n     阿波斯托洛斯·N·阿萨纳萨基斯与本杰明·M·沃尔科夫英译，2013年。","current_english":"“I call upon Proteus,\n key-holding master of the sea,\n first-born, who showed\n the beginnings of all nature,\n changing matter\n into a great variety of forms.\n Honored by all, he is wise,\n and he knows what is now,\n what was before,\n and what will be in the future.\n He has all at his disposal,\n transformed far beyond\n all other immortals\n who dwell on snowy Olympos\n and fly through the air\n and over land and sea,\n for Physis was the first to place\n everything in Proteus.\n Father, attended by holy providence,\n visit the mystic initiates,\n and bring a good end to a life\n of industry and prosperity.”\n    -_The Orphic Hymns_, XXV.\n     trans. Apostolos N. Athanassakis and Benjamin M. {"alias_target":null,"confidence":"high","current_chinese":"\"我们的时光都到了。\n 方才还在，而今已逝。\n 四季不畏惧死神，\n 风、太阳和雨也一样。\n 我们可以像它们那样。\n 来吧宝贝，别畏惧死神。\"\n    -巴克·达摩，Blue Öyster Cult，《（别畏惧）死神》。1976年。","current_english":"“All our times have come.\n Here but now they're gone.\n Seasons don't fear the reaper,\n Nor do the wind, the sun or the rain.\n We can be like they are.\n Come on baby, don't fear the reaper.”\n\n    -Buck Dharma, Blue Öyster Cult, “(Don't Fear) The Reaper”. 1976.","decision_authority":"Current docs/decisions.md literary exceptions; full rereview explicitly distinguishes quotations from gameplay terminology.","deferral_owner":null,"deferral_reason":null,"dependency_group":"Non-unique monsters","display_context":"QuoteDB literary quotation for entity/help display; aliases resolve within the current language namespace before unwrap_desc.","evidence_locations":["crawl-ref/source/dat/descript/quotes.txt:3783","crawl-ref/source/dat/descript/zh/quotes.txt:3179","crawl-ref/source/database.cc@getQuoteString","crawl-ref/source/libutil.cc@unwrap_desc"],"fact_sha256":"c49fe15dfcb793b9d6ca53d7feded7a8c79269d1525958d755c0d5650088814f","glossary_authority":"docs/glossary.md SHA-256 8a36accf4fc362bf8f103d84ba5d5e6639615274e94d38b16a2d2afe0b0c04cf","identity":"quotes:reaper","key":"reaper","lifecycle":"direct-quote","literary_exception_reason":"The quotation personifies Death as the Grim Reaper.","producer_consumer":"database.cc QuoteDB loader and getQuoteString -> unwrap_desc; describe.cc / ability.cc / mutation.cc / lookup-help.cc use canonical English lookup keys.","proposed_translation":null,"reentry_trigger":"Re-review when this quotation, attribution, alias target, literary terminology decision, or display consumer changes.","rejected_alternatives":["未将文学引文强制套入同名游戏机制或实体；非阻断风格建议保留。"],"resolved_key":"reaper","reviewer_rationale":"时光到而逝/季风日雨不惧收割死神、人可如此/对爱人劝不惧的歌完整，文学Reaper死神不机械当怪物名。","section":"Non-unique monsters","suggestions":[],"terminal_conclusion":"keep"}

{"alias_target":null,"confidence":"high","current_chinese":"\"森林里有骚动\n 树木间有纷争\n 因为枫树想要更多阳光\n 而橡树无视它们的恳求\"\n    -Rush，《树》。1978年。","current_english":"“There is unrest in the forest\n There is trouble with the trees\n For the maples want more sunlight\n And the oaks ignore their pleas”\n    -Rush, \"The Trees\". 1978.","decision_authority":"Current docs/decisions.md literary exceptions; full rereview explicitly distinguishes quotations from gameplay terminology.","deferral_owner":null,"deferral_reason":null,"dependency_group":"Non-unique monsters","display_context":"QuoteDB literary quotation for entity/help display; aliases resolve within the current language namespace before unwrap_desc.","evidence_locations":["crawl-ref/source/dat/descript/quotes.txt:3881","crawl-ref/source/dat/descript/zh/quotes.txt:3268","crawl-ref/source/database.cc@getQuoteString","crawl-ref/source/libutil.cc@unwrap_desc"],"fact_sha256":"b0e187b7317de7c93e509c5d8c59e5c48c5e4888cc202368ec063dcc26525adc","glossary_authority":"docs/glossary.md SHA-256 8a36accf4fc362bf8f103d84ba5d5e6639615274e94d38b16a2d2afe0b0c04cf","identity":"quotes:shambling mangrove","key":"shambling mangrove","lifecycle":"direct-quote","literary_exception_reason":null,"producer_consumer":"database.cc QuoteDB loader and getQuoteString -> unwrap_desc; describe.cc / ability.cc / mutation.cc / lookup-help.cc use canonical English lookup keys.","proposed_translation":null,"reentry_trigger":"Re-review when this quotation, attribution, alias target, literary terminology decision, or display consumer changes.","rejected_alternatives":["未将文学引文强制套入同名游戏机制或实体；非阻断风格建议保留。"],"resolved_key":"shambling mangrove","reviewer_rationale":"枫求阳光/橡无视引森林不宁的拟树歌词完整，受害提出请求主体未倒。","section":"Non-unique monsters","suggestions":[],"terminal_conclusion":"keep"}
{"alias_target":null,"confidence":"high","current_chinese":"\"于是那古老的海神从深处\n 爬出，找到了他那肥硕的海豹，\n 审视、清点，却从未接近\n 我们设下的计谋，只当那是五头海豹。\n 他用睡眠舒缓了自己的额角；\n 我们高喊可怖的呼号，一拥而上，\n 奋力用双手从四面八方抱住他；\n 于是那古老的变形者开始施展他所有的形态：\n 首先是一头鬃毛雄壮的狮子，\n 接着是一条龙，然后是一头斑豹，\n 然后是一头巨野猪，又骤然化作\n 一片流水。最后他变成一棵树，\n 树冠卷曲，直冲云霄。\"\n    -荷马，《奥德赛》，第四卷，602-614行。\n     乔治·查普曼英译，1857年。","current_english":"“And then th' old Sea-God crept\n From forth the deeps, and found his fat calves there,\n Survey'd, and number'd, and came never near\n The craft we used, but told us five for calves.\n His temples then dis-eased with sleep he salves;\n And in rush'd we, with an abhorred cry,\n Cast all our hands about him manfully;\n And then th' old Forger all his forms began:\n First was a lion with a mighty mane,\n Then next a dragon, a pied panther then,\n A vast boar next, and suddenly did strain\n All into water. Last he was a tree,\n Curl'd all at top, and shot up to the sky.”\n    -Homer, _The Odyssey_, IV, 602-14.\n     trans. {"alias_target":null,"confidence":"high","current_chinese":"\"我看到一张嘴在嘲讽。熔化的红铁般的笑容从上面掠过。它\n 的笑声满是钉子叮当碰撞。那是孩子梦中才会出现的嘴。\n 一只拳头击中了那张嘴：由电动的腕和肩驱动的炮铜指节。\n 那是孩子梦中才会出现的手臂。\n 拳头一次又一次、一遍又一遍地击打着那张嘴。嘴里流出\n 熔化的铁血，发出钉子叮当碰撞的笑声。\n 而我看到，拳头捶打得越狠，那张嘴笑得越响。拳头不停地\n 捶打着，捶打着，嘴巴回应着。\"\n    -卡尔·桑德堡，《滴水兽》，《玉米剥皮者》。1918年。","current_english":"“I saw a mouth jeering. A smile of melted red iron ran over it. Its laugh was\n full of nails rattling. It was a child's dream of an arm.\n The fist hit the mouth over and over, again and again. The mouth bled melted\n iron, and laughed its laughter of nails rattling.\n And I saw the more the fist pounded the more the mouth laughed. {"alias_target":null,"confidence":"high","current_chinese":"\"说吧！说吧！你这可怕的来客！\n 你胸中空空，\n 却仍披着粗陋的战甲，\n 前来惊吓我！\n 未曾裹以东方香膏，\n 却伸出你无肉的掌心，\n 仿佛在乞求施舍，\n 你为何萦绕我不散？\"\n    -亨利·沃兹沃思·朗费罗，《披甲骷髅》。1841年。","current_english":"“Speak! speak! thou fearful guest!\n Who, with thy hollow breast\n Still in rude armor drest,\n Comest to daunt me!\n Wrapt not in Eastern balms,\n But with thy fleshless palms\n Stretched, as if asking alms,\n Why dost thou haunt me?”\n    -Henry Wadsworth Longfellow, “The Skeleton in Armor”. 1841.","decision_authority":"Current docs/decisions.md literary exceptions; full rereview explicitly distinguishes quotations from gameplay terminology.","deferral_owner":null,"deferral_reason":null,"dependency_group":"Non-unique monsters","display_context":"QuoteDB literary quotation for entity/help display; aliases resolve within the current language namespace before unwrap_desc.","evidence_locations":["crawl-ref/source/dat/descript/quotes.txt:3934","crawl-ref/source/dat/descript/zh/quotes.txt:3321","crawl-ref/source/database.cc@getQuoteString","crawl-ref/source/libutil.cc@unwrap_desc"],"fact_sha256":"896030fd777fb5a6dc75483a6a31bbfc5bcf119b3cedcb10d77739c6f32c836b","glossary_authority":"docs/glossary.md SHA-256 8a36accf4fc362bf8f103d84ba5d5e6639615274e94d38b16a2d2afe0b0c04cf","identity":"quotes:skeletal warrior","key":"skeletal warrior","lifecycle":"direct-quote","literary_exception_reason":null,"producer_consumer":"database.cc QuoteDB loader and getQuoteString -> unwrap_desc; describe.cc / ability.cc / mutation.cc / lookup-help.cc use canonical English lookup keys.","proposed_translation":null,"reentry_trigger":"Re-review when this quotation, attribution, alias target, literary terminology decision, or display consumer changes.","rejected_alternatives":["未将文学引文强制套入同名游戏机制或实体；非阻断风格建议保留。"],"resolved_key":"skeletal warrior","reviewer_rationale":"空胸粗甲幽客/非东方防腐香/无肉掌如乞/求答为何缠的诗意与问题完整。","section":"Non-unique monsters","suggestions":[],"terminal_conclusion":"keep"}

{"alias_target":null,"confidence":"high","current_chinese":"\"走了一阵，他们来到了一个村庄。'好吧，'鳄龟说，\n '朋友们，天亮时分，我们就发起进攻。我先去那个地方。'\n 战团的首领对他们说道。\n\n '好，'另一个小家伙说，'你是决定我们该做什么的人，'\n 他们对那只鳄龟说道。'好吧，'鳄龟说，'现在我要\n 告诉你们我该做什么。'他这样说道。'现在，我要开始\n 朝这个村子走了。等我杀死酋长的女儿时，天正好破晓，\n 与此同时，明日来临的方向天空会染红。'嗬，那边，我们\n 的同伴杀了她！'——你们心里要这样想。那时就是你们发出\n 巨大声响的时刻，你们要不停地呐喊。现在就是你们去攻打\n 这个村子的时候。'他如此对他那些年轻人说道。\n\n '好的！'其他小家伙们说道。\"\n    -《鳄龟出征记》，《美国民族学学会出版物，第九卷：\n     基卡普故事集》。1915年。\n     杜鲁门·迈克尔逊英译。","current_english":"“After a while they came to a village. ”Now then,“ said Snapping Turtle, ”in\n the morning at daylight, my friends, we will make on attack. I myself will\n first go to the place,“ the leader of the war party said to them.\n\n ”Good,“ said the other little one, ”thou art the one who sees to it what we\n shall do,“ they said to that Snapping Turtle. ”Now then,“ said Snapping\n Turtle, ”verily I am now going to tell you what I shall do.“ Thus he spoke.\n ”Now is the time I shall begin to walk toward this village. Verily at the time\n I shall kill the daughter of the chief will be when the light of day is\n breaking, and at the same instant the sky will glow with red in the direction\n whence the morrow comes. ‘Ho, there, our comrade has killed her!’ will thus be\n the thought in your hearts. {"alias_target":null,"confidence":"high","current_chinese":"\"在任何组合中，固体叙述着由虚空生成的异常，或者说，\n 虚空对固体的感染（当虚空抵达固体时，它作用为一种缠绕\n 的瘟疫，一种盘卷翻腾的传染病，而非一种消除过程或固体\n 湮灭剂）；在组合中，没有纯粹的固体，只有被玷污的、\n 染病和被摧残的固体。\n ［……］\n 固体能够启动其构造和组合活动（生存、发展等过程）的\n 唯一方式，就是让虚空进入。固体的动态特征只有在被虚空\n 吞噬、缠绕和搅乱时才能被激活。固体别无选择。\"\n    -雷扎·内加雷斯塔尼，《旋风学：与匿名物质的共谋》。2008年。","current_english":"“In any composition, the solid narrates the anomalies generated by the void, or\n the infection of the void through the solid (where the void comes to the solid,\n it works as a convoluting plague, a coiling swirling epidemic rather than a\n nullifying process or a solid-annihilating agent); in a composition there is no\n pure solid but a defiled one, a diseased and deflowered solid.\n [...]\n The only way that the solid can initialize its architectonic and compositional\n activities (processes for survival, development, etc.) is by letting the void\n in. {"alias_target":null,"confidence":"high","current_chinese":"\"另一边，泰坦们也急切地加强阵势，双方同时展示着他们\n 双手的力量和威力。无边的海洋可怖地咆哮，大地轰然作响：\n 辽阔的天空颤抖呻吟，高耸的奥林匹斯山在永生众神的冲击\n 下从根基动摇，沉重的震撼直达幽暗的塔耳塔罗斯，还有\n 他们在那可怕的突袭和猛烈投石中沉重的脚步声。于是，\n 他们彼此投掷着致命的飞弹，两军呐喊的呼声直达星空；\n 他们以惊天动地的战吼交汇在一起。\"\n    -赫西俄德，《神谱》，公元前8世纪。\n     H.G.伊夫林-怀特英译，1914年。","current_english":"“And on the other part the Titans eagerly strengthened their ranks, and both\n sides at one time showed the work of their hands and their might. {"alias_target":null,"confidence":"high","current_chinese":"\"我对19世纪末那个问题'电动力学想告诉我们什么'的完整\n 回答，简单来说就是：\n\n 虚空中的场具有物理实在性；支撑它们的介质则没有。\n\n 在消除了电动力学的神秘之后，请允许我立即对量子力学\n 做同样的事：\n\n 关联具有物理实在性；被关联的事物则没有。\"\n    -N.大卫·默明，《量子力学想告诉我们什么？》，1998年。","current_english":"“My complete answer to the late 19th century question 'what is electrodynamics\n trying to tell us' would simply be this:\n\n Fields in empty space have physical reality; the medium that supports them does\n not.\n\n Having thus removed the mystery from electrodynamics, let me immediately do the\n same for quantum mechanics:\n\n Correlations have physical reality; that which they correlate does not.”\n    -N.
